text:
maria: quick thought — we should add a soft failover path that kicks in when the primary model is saturated (by capacity/queue length) and route to a cheaper quantized variant for non-SLA tiers. This would reduce 5xx/queueing without breaking gold-tier SLOs.

akshay: +1, but need to be careful with cost accounting and quotas. If we route gold users to cheaper variants without telling them it could violate contracts. Maybe restrict auto-fallback to standard/free tiers and explicitly opt-in for gold?

zheng: technical constraints: we currently have per-model queue depth and active GPU slots metrics. We can trigger fallback when active_slots/utilization > 0.9 OR avg-queue-ms > 2000 for 30s. That should avoid flapping.

maria: exactly. proposal sketch:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  match:
    - tier: free|standard
    - region: any
  trigger:
    - metric: gpu_utilization
      threshold: 0.9
      window: 30s
  fallback_sequence:
    - model: model-x-q8
      max_latency_increase_ms: 150
    - model: model-x-q4
      max_latency_increase_ms: 300
  telemetry:
    emit: [fallback_count, fallback_latency_delta_ms, original_model_token_cost]
```

sophie: from a console UX POV we need to show: live fallback status, per-route fallback rate, per-tenant impact, and a clear toggle (auto vs manual). Also a way to surface hallucination/regression alerts if fallback impacts quality.

ira: +1 on the quality telemetry. add an evaluated prompt set run when a tenant sees >1% fallback rate in 24h. If quality regression > threshold -> block auto-fallback and notify SRE/SE.

akshay: ops question — what about cross-region spillover? If region A is saturated and we route to a variant in region B, need to respect data residency. We should default to local-region fallbacks only, and if none available then failover to local cheaper variant.

zheng: implementation notes: runtime can maintain a per-route state machine: NORMAL -> SOFT_FAILOVER -> HARD_FAILOVER. SOFT_FAILOVER uses cheaper variant same region; HARD_FAILOVER only for non-sensitive tenants and after explicit consent. We'll add hysteresis: cool-down 5m before revert.

maria: also add per-tenant opt-out via API:
`PATCH /routing-configs/{tenant}` body: {"auto_fallback": false} — default true for standard/free, false for enterprise.

sophie: console should expose last 24h fallback events + reason code (utilization, queue, health-check). And add a clear audit log entry so sales/CS can explain to customers.

akshay: need to update billing pipeline: when fallback happens, tag tokens with model_variant so cost can be attributed. Otherwise finance will see mismatches.

zheng: will prototype the state machine and emit metrics: routing.fallback.count, routing.fallback.latency_delta_ms, routing.fallback.quality_alerts. I'll throw a small endpoint for querying tenant fallback history.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/fallback-proto -> canary tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

maria: nice — next steps: zheng to prototype, sophie to mock console widgets, akshay/ira to write safety rules (residency/quota/billing), i'll draft a short RFC. Ping me if you want to pair on the RFC. :+1:

akshay: leaving one note — make sure fallback doesn't change the model signature (functions/schema) — if the cheaper variant lacks function-calling support we must not silently downgrade for function-heavy requests.

zheng: good catch. add model capability check to the trigger: only fallback to variants that are function-compatible with the original request.

maria: perfect. thanks all.
